# LogarithmInvalidRealDomain

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Use a positive logarithm argument.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$n = log(-7);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use a positive logarithm argument.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- log, log10 or log1p has a proven numeric value outside its real-valued finite-result domain: log/log10 argument <= 0; log1p argument <= -1. Also report log base <= 0 or equal to 1 when explicit.
- Resolve builtin functions, extension classes, constants and method receivers, including aliases and supported named arguments. Inspect reachable operations in one lexical scope with bounded local flow.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Never infer policy from names or comments. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Exclude shadowed or unresolved symbols, incomplete code, unknown required constants, ambiguous receiver identity and unsupported versions. Reassignment, escaping aliases, and unknown calls invalidate dependent flow facts.
- An argument written directly as a number literal at the edge of the domain (`log(0)`, `log10(0.0)`, `-log(0)` for +INF, `log1p(-1)`, parentheses allowed) is not reported: PHP returns -INF without a warning, and code spells it out to get an infinity. The same value reached through a variable or a computation, any value past the edge, and an invalid base stay reported.
- Both @custos-ignore LogarithmInvalidRealDomain and @noinspection LogarithmInvalidRealDomain suppress this native rule.

## Fix

None. A safe repair requires choosing values, error handling, or application behavior.

## PHP versions

Apply throughout PHP 5.3–8.5 only where the extension API and syntax exist.  Do not flag API unavailability through this rule.

## Options

None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "LogarithmInvalidRealDomain": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore LogarithmInvalidRealDomain
```
